number.why: The reported primary composite HR is 0.77 with 95% CI 0.61–0.96 for colchicine versus placebo. Follow-up was a median of 22.6 months; the registry specifies first events assessed up to 3.5 years. Agreement includes the ruling's qualification that intention-to-treat is not explicitly established by the held sources; numerical confirmation does not verify that served population label.

quotes.span: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, resuscitated cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent hospitalization for angina leading to coronary revascularization.

The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02).
Patients were followed for a median of 22.6 months.

entry.why: Eligibility explicitly requires adults with documented acute myocardial infarction within 30 days. The abstract establishes randomized, double-blind comparison of low-dose colchicine with placebo, satisfying the packet's question. The unresolved analysis-set label does not undermine entry-population eligibility.

quotes.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Males and females of at least 18 years of age capable and willing to provide informed consent * Patient must have suffered a documented acute myocardial infarction within the last 30 days

We performed a randomized, double-blind trial involving patients recruited within 30 days after a myocardial infarction. The patients were randomly assigned to receive either low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg once daily) or placebo.

missed: No additional finding changes either ruling. Numerical agreement remains conditional on preserving the ruling's explicit qualification that the served intention-to-treat label is unverified.
